sc: Rash after amoxicillin in a child with tonsillitis and a big spleen → EBV, not penicillin allergy
Jaundiced neonate needs a cephalosporin → Cefotaxime (not ceftriaxone)
Weak legs after many salbutamol nebulisers → Hypokalaemia
f: Dose per kg, never above the adult dose · weight estimate (1–10 yr): (age + 4) × 2 · check renal function, age limits
Amoxicillin 40–45 mg/kg 12-hourly · ampicillin 50 mg/kg 6-hourly · gentamicin 7.5 mg/kg daily · ceftriaxone 50–100 mg/kg · ciprofloxacin 15 mg/kg 12-hourly
Paracetamol 15 mg/kg 6-hourly (max 60 mg/kg/day) · ibuprofen 5–10 mg/kg 8-hourly (not in chickenpox) · morphine 0.1–0.2 mg/kg
10% dextrose 5 ml/kg · adrenaline 10 µg/kg (IV 1:10 000 in arrest, IM 1:1000 in anaphylaxis) · Ca gluconate 10% 0.5 ml/kg · diazepam 0.3 IV / 0.5 PR
Aspirin (Reye) · tetracycline < 8 yr (teeth) · chloramphenicol in neonates (grey baby) · ceftriaxone in jaundiced neonates · propranolol in wheeze
Aminoglycosides: ototoxicity, nephrotoxicity · erythromycin in newborns: pyloric stenosis · vancomycin: red man · primaquine, cotrimoxazole: G6PD haemolysis
trap: Hypoglycaemia: 10% dextrose, not 50% · anaphylaxis: 1:1000 IM, not 1:10 000 IV · no furosemide for kwashiorkor oedema · black stools on iron are expected
